title: Value Used for the Rural Home Loans Escrow Waiver Limit — Collateral Valuation Standard
content:
**Standard.** For a Rural Home Loans loan, the value the escrow waiver loan-to-value limit is applied to is chosen from the homesite's history with the Farm Real Estate Loans parcels and from its acreage.

## Rule

The value the limit is applied to is chosen as follows: when the homesite was released from a farm real estate mortgage as a farmstead split, the value is the lower of the home's original value and the appraised value recorded at that release; when the homesite is larger than 20 acres, the value is the original value less 5 percent; otherwise it is the original value.

## Records relied on

- **Farmstead split:** a parcel release on the Farm Real Estate Loans parcel records for the homesite's county parcel number, with the release reason farmstead split; the appraised value is the one recorded with that release (the latest such release).
- **Acreage:** the deeded acres of the homesite on the loan record.
- **Original value:** the original value on the loan record.

## Decision table

| Released as a farmstead split | Homesite acres | Value |
|---|---|---|
| yes | any | the lower of the original value and the release appraisal |
| no | more than 20 | the original value less 5 percent of it |
| no | 20 or fewer | the original value |

## Worked figures (hypothetical homesites)

- Original value 320000.00, released as a farmstead split with an appraisal of 305000.00 at release: the value is 305000.00. Had the release appraisal been 340000.00, the value would be 320000.00.
- Original value 320000.00, 24 acres, never part of a farm mortgage: 320000.00 less 5 percent, that is 304000.00.
- Original value 320000.00, exactly 20 acres: 320000.00.
